items.name: org-chart
items.title: Org Chart
items.description: An interactive organization chart on the workspace canvas: automatic top-down layout, pan and zoom, folding teams, a details panel, drag-to-reassign with a live preview wire, and a searchable change-manager dialog for keyboard users.
items.docs:
Import from `@/components/ui/org-chart`. Lays out flat reporting lines as a top-down tree on a pannable, zoomable canvas. The chart owns layout, the viewport, folding, selection, and its details panel; the host owns the people and persists every move, edit, and removal through callbacks. The canvas is 600px tall by default; pass `className="h-full"` inside a bounded parent to fill it instead: ```tsx 'use client'; import { OrgChart, type OrgChartEdge } from '@/components/ui/org-chart'; const edges: OrgChartEdge[] = [ { id: 'alex', parentId: null, displayName: 'Alex Morgan', positionTitle: 'CEO', avatarUrl: null }, { id: 'sam', parentId: 'alex', displayName: 'Sam Rivera', positionTitle: 'VP Product', avatarUrl: null }, ];
saveManager(childId, newParentId)} onEditNode={(person) => openPositionEditor(person.id)} onRemoveNode={(person) => confirmRemoval(person.id)} />
``` Every `OrgChartEdge` key is required: `id`, `parentId` (null for a root), and the nullable `displayName`, `avatarUrl`, and `positionTitle`. Anyone whose manager is missing becomes a root and a cycle is broken, so bad data still shows everyone once. - Pass exactly one of `edges` or `defaultEdges`. With `edges` the chart is controlled and only changes when you pass new edges, so update them after `onReparent`. With `defaultEdges` it moves the card at once and moves it back if `onReparent` throws or rejects; new `defaultEdges` content resets it. - `onReparent(childId, newParentId, preserve: { positionTitle?: string | null }) => void | Promise` fires on a drop onto a new manager or from the Change manager dialog. Moving someone under their own report is refused before it fires. - `onReparentSuccess(childName, parentName)` and `onReparentError(message)` are for your toasts; the chart shows none. - `onEditNode(node)` and `onRemoveNode(node)` add Edit position and Remove from chart to the card menu and details panel, and receive an `OrgChartNodeData`: the edge plus `childCount`, `isRoot`, and `isCompact`. Removal only reports intent, so confirm before changing data. - `onAddToChart()` adds an "Add first person" button to the empty state shown when there are no edges. - `editable` (default true) enables dragging and the card menu; `isLoading` shows a loading state; `showDetails` (default true) shows the details panel; `onSelectNode(node | null)` reports selection so you can render your own panel; `defaultCollapsedIds` folds those people's teams at first render. Tab into the chart and use the arrow keys to move between people; Enter opens their details.

items.name: workspace-kit
items.title: Workspace Kit
items.description: The shared workspace shell behind the application templates: a collapsible sidebar rail with a mobile drawer, nav rows and sections, 48px view headers and scrolling view frames, filter pills, segmented controls, surfaces that keep their edge in dark mode (panels, table surfaces, stat tiles, key-value lists, empty states), a pan-and-zoom canvas with double-framed nodes and bezier wires, and a React ViewTransition wrapper with a reduced-motion fallback.
items.docs:
Import everything from `@/components/ui/workspace-kit`. The shell, views, and surfaces the application templates are built from; all presentational, so the host owns data, routing, and state. Views size themselves to the container they get (container queries), not the viewport. App shell with a sidebar and one view: ```tsx import { Inbox, Rows3 } from 'lucide-react'; import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'; import { NavIcon, NavRow, NavSection, Panel, SidebarFrame, ToneBadge, ViewFrame, WorkspaceShell } from '@/components/ui/workspace-kit';
( Acme} collapsed={collapsed} onCollapsedChange={onCollapsedChange} drawer={mode === 'drawer'} onClose={onNavigate}> } onClick={onNavigate} /> )} > New order}> …
``` The `sidebar` render prop is called twice: as the rail (from the `3xl` container width) and inside the mobile drawer; call `onNavigate` after a choice so the drawer closes. Shell and navigation: - `WorkspaceShell` (`sidebar(props)`, children, `defaultSidebarCollapsed`, `framed` for a rounded app window, `slot`): fills its parent, so give the parent a height. - `SidebarFrame` (`label`, `menu` (top-left switcher), `collapsed`, `onCollapsedChange`, `drawer`, `onClose`, `footer`); `NavSection` (`title`, `collapsed`, `action`); `NavRow` (`label`, `collapsed`, `active`, `leading`, `trailing`, `href` + `renderLink(props)` for your router's link, or `onClick`; `busy`, `disabled`, `muted`); `NavIcon` (`icon`, `active`); `NavCount` (`value`, `tone`: muted | warning | danger); `RailTip` labels a rail control. - `SwitcherTrigger` (`label`, `name`, `glyph`, `collapsed`) and `monogram(name)` build the top-left switcher; `AppearanceRow` (`value`, `onChange`: light | dark | system) is the theme row for a menu. Views: - `ViewFrame` (`icon`, `title`, `actions`, `label`, `maxWidth` default `max-w-6xl`): a 48px header over a scrolling, centred column. `ViewHeader` (`icon`, `title`, children = actions, `divider`) is the header alone; `NavMenuButton` opens the drawer on narrow widths and is already in both. - `SectionHeading` (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `id`) separates groups of panels in a view. - `SearchField` (`label` (visually hidden), `trailing`, `inputRef`, plus input props such as `value`, `onChange`, `placeholder`): the compact toolbar search. - `FilterGroup` (`label`, `value`, `options: { value, label, count?, icon? }[]`, `onChange`, `compact`): single-choice filter pills that scroll sideways when narrow, e.g. ``. - `Segmented` (`label`, `value`, `options: { value, label, icon? }[]`, `onChange`): a two-to-four option switch, e.g. ``. - `TooltipIconButton` (`label` (required, also the accessible name), `side`, `variant`: ghost | raised, `size`: sm | md | lg, `onClick`, icon as children). Surfaces: - `Panel` (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `footer`, `bodyClassName` (`p-0` for edge-to-edge content)): the standard card. - `TableSurface` (`minWidth` default `40rem`, below which it scrolls sideways): wraps table rows; style them with `tableHeadClass`, `tableRowClass`, and `tableGroupRowClass`, e.g. `NameAda`. - `StatTile` (`label`, `value`, `hint`, `icon`): a label over a large figure; lay several in a grid inside a `Panel` or `Bezel`. - `KeyValueList` (`items: { label, value, key? }[]`): label-value rows with dashed rules. - `EmptyState` (`icon` (required), `title`, `description`, `action`): a centred empty, no-match, or error state. - `ToneBadge` (`tone`: neutral | primary | info | success | warning | danger | violet | amber, children, `onClick` makes it a button), e.g. `Paid`; `StatusBadge` (`presentation: { label, tone }`) maps a status to one; `TONE_COLOR` gives each tone's CSS colour. - `IconTile` (`icon`, `tone`): a tinted glyph tile for rows and notices. `Bezel` (`muted`, `innerClassName`): a double-framed card for highlighted content. - `MiddleTruncate` (`text`, `tail` (characters kept at the end), `title`): shortens long names and keys in the middle, keeping their ending. Helpers: `formatCount(n, locale?)`, `plural(n, { one, other })`, `nameList(names, { max })`; `useScrollFade()` fades the edges of a sideways scroller; `focusRingClass`, `pressClass`, `hitAreaClass`, `dashedRule`, `nativeSelectClass`, `scrollRowClass`, `surfaceInsetClass` + `SurfaceBody` are the shared class names; `enterClass` + `staggerStyle(i)` stagger entrances; `useReducedMotion()`; `ViewAnimation` and `startViewTransition(update, ...types)` animate view swaps where supported (React 19.3) and fall back to an instant swap. Canvas (pan and zoom diagrams): `useCanvasViewport(contentWidth, { fit, contentHeight, minZoom, maxZoom })` returns the viewport for `CanvasSurface` (`viewport`, `label`, children in canvas units, `overlay`, `onPaneClick`) and `CanvasZoomControls` (`viewport`, `fit`); draw nodes with `NodeShell` (`tone`: plain | new | target, `selected`) and `NodeIconTile`, and links with `CanvasWire` (`start` and `end` as `[x, y]`, `tone`: rest | live | warn, `axis`, `animated`) or `wirePath(start, end)`.

items.description: A coding agent workspace template: sessions in a tab strip or a project sidebar, each with a chat transcript, a resizable side panel for reviewing diffs, reading files, previewing the app, following the session's other agents and its shared tasks, and a terminal dock. Sub-agents, orchestrator/worker runs and messages between agents show in the transcript, and sessions flag when any of their agents needs an answer.
items.docs: Import: `import { CodingAgent, CODING_AGENT_DEMO, createHarnessStore } from '@/components/ui/coding-agent'`. Pass your own `data`, handle side effects through `onAction`, and draw your app in the browser tab with `renderBrowserPage`. Each session plays a `script`, or shows a real harness: pass an `events` log, or a store from `createHarnessStore()` and push events as they happen. Sub-agents, messages between agents, handoffs, phases, shared tasks, worktrees, pull requests and CI checks are all events.

items.name: data-rooms
items.title: Data Rooms
items.description: Secure document rooms for an organization and its sub-organizations: access that carries down the hierarchy, expiring folder shares, agreements before entry, view-only and watermarked documents, Q&A, reading insights, an access map, and a room assistant that only cites what the reader can open.
items.docs:
Import from `@/components/ui/data-rooms`. Document rooms for an organization and its sub-units, driven by one `data` object: the block owns navigation, dialogs, the viewer, and applying changes you accept; the host owns storage, file delivery, authorization, and the activity log. Its access rules only pick which controls appear; your server decides every request. It fills its parent, so give the parent a bounded height: ```tsx 'use client'; import { DataRooms, type DataRoomsData } from '@/components/ui/data-rooms'; const at = '2026-09-30T10:00:00Z'; const data: DataRoomsData = { clock: '2026-10-01T09:00:00Z', // "now" for dates and expiries org: { name: 'Acme' }, viewerId: 'ada', people: [{ id: 'ada', name: 'Ada Park', email: 'ada@acme.com' }], units: [{ id: 'acme', parentId: null, name: 'Acme', kind: 'Company' }], // exactly one root roles: [{ id: 'viewer', name: 'Viewer', permissions: ['view', 'download'], isDefault: true }], memberships: [{ id: 'm1', personId: 'ada', scope: { kind: 'unit', id: 'acme' }, owner: true, status: 'active' }], inheritance: { owners: true, admins: true, members: false, allowGuests: true }, rooms: [{ id: 'board', unitId: 'acme', name: 'Board pack', status: 'active', createdAt: at, policies: { viewOnly: false, watermark: true, requireAgreement: false, restricted: false } }], documents: [{ id: 'q3', roomId: 'board', folder: '/Financials', name: 'Q3.pdf', kind: 'pdf', size: 482000, uploadedBy: 'ada', updatedAt: at, versions: [{ id: 'v1', number: 1, uploadedBy: 'ada', uploadedAt: at, size: 482000 }] }], shares: [], invites: [], acceptances: [], activity: [], questions: [], };
save(command)} onAction={(action) => track(action)} />
``` `DATA_ROOMS_DEMO` is a complete example. - `onCommand(command) => Promise | void` makes every change: resolve once saved and the block applies it until you pass new `data`, or reject with an `Error` to keep the dialog open with its message. It isn't called while previewing as someone else. Types: `create-room { room }`, `update-room { roomId, patch }`, `invite { roomId, invites: { email, personId? }[], roleId, expiresAt?, message? }`, `revoke-invite { inviteId }`, `update-membership { membershipId, patch }`, `remove-membership { membershipId }`, `create-share { roomId, folder, personIds, can: { view, edit, delete }, expiresAt? }`, `revoke-share { shareId }`, `upload { roomId, folder, files: { name, size, kind, pages? }[] }` (metadata only, no bytes), `create-folder { roomId, path }`, `move-documents { documentIds, folder }`, `update-document { documentId, patch: { restrictions } }`, `update-inheritance { inheritance }`, `save-role { role }`, `accept-agreement { roomId, version }`, `ask-question { roomId, documentId?, title, body }`, `answer-question { questionId, body, close? }`, `set-question-status { questionId, status }`. - `onAction(action)`: `download { documentId, versionId? }`, `view-document { documentId }` (for your access log), `export-activity { roomId? }`, `search { query }`, `contact { personId }`, `org-menu { item: 'organization-settings' | 'profile' | 'support' | 'log-out' }`. - `onAskAssistant({ roomId, prompt, viewerId, documentId? })` resolves to `{ text, citations: { documentId, page?, quote? }[] }`; cite only what the asker can open. Without it, `data.assistant` answers. - `renderPreview(document, { viewer, watermark, viewOnly }) => ReactNode` draws viewer pages instead of placeholders. - `view` (`'home' | 'access-map' | 'activity' | 'room'`), `roomId`, `tab` (`'documents' | 'people' | 'questions' | 'insights' | 'settings'`), and `previewAs` (person id or null) each have a `default…` prop and an `on…Change`; `views` limits navigation. - `theme` / `onThemeChange` (menu switch only), `defaultSidebarCollapsed`, `framed`, `locale` / `timeZone` (default en-US, UTC), `className`.

items.name: billing-kit
items.title: Billing Kit
items.description: Contracts, formatters, provider descriptors (Stripe built in), and components for Constructive billing: plans and prices, meters in the credit waterfall, balances, credit grants and packs, gift codes (redeem, create, bulk batches, redemptions), limits and feature caps, the ledger, invoices, provider readiness, customers, and database standing.
items.docs: Import: `import { BillingFormatProvider, CurrentPlanCard, UsageTree, PlanChangeDialog, STRIPE_PROVIDER } from '@/components/ui/billing-kit'`. Wrap components in `BillingFormatProvider` with a locale, time zone, and a fixed `now` from the server. Money is integer minor units and `-1` means unlimited, as in the database. Register more payment providers by passing your own `BillingProviderDescriptor` objects; `logo`, `modeLabels`, `detectMode`, `merchantOfRecord`, and `immutablePrices` cover what differs between providers.

items.name: billing-account
items.title: Billing Account
items.description: The customer billing workspace: an account switcher and six views (overview, usage, plans, credits, invoices, activity) over one account’s plan, credit waterfall, credits, invoices, and ledger, with a plan-change preview and provider-neutral actions.
items.docs: Import: `import { BillingAccount, BILLING_ACCOUNT_DEMO } from '@/components/ui/billing-account'`. Pass `data` mapped from your billing tables and hand purchases to your payment provider through `onChangePlan`, `onBuyCredits`, `onRedeemCode`, and `onAction`; limit `views` to what your data can back. Fill `paymentMethod` from your provider to show the method on file.

items.name: billing-console
items.title: Billing Console
items.description: The operator billing workspace for the platform or a tenant database: overview, catalog (plans and prices, entitlement matrix, meters, packs and codes), customers with credit grants, the payment provider with readiness and the gated billing switch, and platform database standing.
items.docs: Import: `import { BillingConsole, BILLING_CONSOLE_DEMO } from '@/components/ui/billing-console'`. Pass `data` for one billing module and route every write through the callbacks (`onSaveEntitlements`, `onConnectProvider`, `onRunReadinessCheck`, `onToggleBilling`, `onGrantCredits`, `onHoldDatabase`, and more). Credentials are write-only.

items.name: resource-kit
items.title: Resource Kit
items.description: List, detail, and form screens generated from resource definitions: a view with search, sort, pagination, and empty and error states; a table that formats cells by field, shows option badges and relation labels, and folds columns in narrow panes; a create and edit sheet with validation, async relation pickers, and many-to-many links; a record view with has-many lists; and delete confirmation. Backend-neutral: data goes through an injected source, routing through an injected router.
items.docs: Import: `import { ResourceKitProvider, ResourcePage, RecordDetail, defineResource } from '@/components/ui/resource-kit'`. Describe each table with `defineResource({ name, label, singular, primaryKey, titleField, columns, formFields, fields, source })`, where `source` implements `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `remove`, and optionally `link` and `linked` for many-to-many fields. Wrap the app once in `<ResourceKitProvider router={{ Link, navigate, listHref, detailHref }} resources={[...]} icons={{ users: Users }}>` (it reuses an enclosing QueryClient or makes its own), then render `<ResourcePage resource="contacts" />` on the list route and `<RecordDetail resource="contacts" id={id} />` on the detail route. Writes invalidate the resource and every related one. `DataTable`, `EntityFormSheet`, `RelationPicker`, `DeleteDialog`, `ResourceNav`, and `createMemorySource` are exported for custom screens and prototypes.

items.name: auth-pages
items.title: Auth Pages
items.description: Public account screens for an app: sign-in, sign-up, check-email, verify-email, forgot-password, and reset-password panels and a centred page layout, with field validation, pending and failure states, and injected handlers that answer `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, message }`, so they work with any router and any auth backend.
items.docs: Import: `import { AuthLayout, SignInPanel, SignUpPanel, VerifyEmailPanel } from '@/components/ui/auth-pages'`. Render one panel per route inside `AuthLayout`, pass your auth calls as handlers that return `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, message }`, and pass your router's link once as `linkComponent` on the layout. Navigate after sign-in succeeds yourself; sign-up never expects a session and shows the check-email state instead.

items.name: dashboard-tiles
items.title: Dashboard Tiles
items.description: Dashboard pieces for a resource-kit app: a stat tile on its own card that can link to its source, a count tile that reads a resource total (optionally filtered), the latest records of a resource, and a grid that lays them out by its own width.
items.docs: Import: `import { DashboardGrid, ResourceCountTile, RecentRecords, StatTile } from '@/components/ui/dashboard-tiles'`. Render inside `ResourceKitProvider`: `<DashboardGrid><ResourceCountTile resource="deals" label="Open deals" filters={{ status: 'open' }} /><StatTile label="Revenue" value="$48,210" hint="This month" href="/invoices" /><RecentRecords resource="contacts" limit={5} /></DashboardGrid>`. Count tiles read `totalCount` from one-row `list` calls; `RecentRecords` follows the resource's `defaultSort` (or `createdAt` descending when there is none); pass `sort` to choose. `StatTile` also works without the provider.

items.name: ai
items.title: AI Kit
items.description: Presentational primitives for AI chat and agent UIs: a chat transcript of user and assistant messages in a conversation thread, with markdown and streaming, a composer (prompt input), conversation scrolling, reasoning, tool calls, human-in-the-loop approval, plan tracking, sources, and streaming surfaces for an assistant or agent conversation.
items.docs:
Import from `@/components/ui/ai` (the `ai` directory under your shadcn ui alias). Presentational only: the host owns the messages, streaming state, tool results, and model calls, and passes them in as props; there is no data hook. Transcript and composer, in a flex column with a bounded height (ChatContainer scrolls itself and sticks to the bottom while new content arrives, so give it `min-h-0 flex-1`; ScrollButton must sit inside it): ```tsx import { ArrowUp } from 'lucide-react'; import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'; import { ChatContainer, ChatContainerContent, Message, MessageAvatar, MessageContent, PromptInput, PromptInputAction, PromptInputActions, PromptInputBody, PromptInputTextarea, ScrollButton } from '@/components/ui/ai';
{messages.map((m) => ( {m.role === 'assistant' ? : null} {m.text} ))}
``` PromptInput is controlled with `value`/`onValueChange` (uncontrolled without them); Enter calls `onSubmit`, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, and the textarea grows to `maxHeight` (240px). `isLoading` or `disabled` disables the textarea; render your own Stop button in PromptInputActions while a run streams. MessageContent renders plain text by default; `markdown` renders markdown with code blocks, and `streaming` throttles those re-renders while tokens arrive. MessageActions/MessageAction (`tooltip`) hold per-message buttons; FeedbackBar (`onCopy`, `onRegenerate`, `onFeedback`) is a ready-made row of them. SystemMessage (`title`) is a centred notice in the transcript. Other families, each a controlled view of host state: - Tool (`name`, `status`: pending | running | success | error | aborted, or the input-/output- stream statuses; `summary`, `input`, `output`, `errorText`), grouped in ToolGroup (`label`). ToolTrace (`title`, `steps`) is a compact multi-step trace. - Reasoning (`content` or children, `isStreaming`, `durationMs`, `markdown`) is the collapsible thinking block; ThinkingBar (`text`, `onStop`) is the one-line live variant; ThinkingStatus (`label`, `elapsedSeconds`, `tokens`) shows elapsed time and tokens. - ThinkingTrace (`rows`, `mode`: steps | reasoning | search | coding, `isStreaming`) lists trace rows; Steps/Step (`title`, `status`: pending | running | done | error) is a collapsible checklist, also exported as ChainOfThought. - ApprovalCard (`title`, `description`, `questions`, `preview`, `destructive`, `onConfirm({ answers })`, `onSkip`) asks a person before a tool runs. - PlanTracker (`plan: { steps: { label, status: pending | in_progress | done }[] }`, `streaming`) pins the agent's plan above the composer; TaskList/TaskRow (`label`, `status`: pending | running | completed | failed, `progress`, `details`, `onRetry`) lists background tasks. - Sources/Source (`href`, `title`, `domain`, `favicon`) cite links; ContextCards/ContextCard (`title`, `body`, `sourceName`) show retrieved context; RecommendationCard (`body`, `confidence`, `alternatives`, `onAccept`) offers a choice. - MessageContent with `streaming` is the default for live replies. ResponseStream (`text`, `mode`: typewriter | fade) animates text you already have in full, e.g. a replayed reply; StreamingText (`text` or `tokens`, `streaming`, `sources`, `followUps`) is a self-contained answer with citations and follow-ups. useThrottledText throttles your own token renders. - PromptSuggestions/PromptSuggestion (`onClick`) offer starter prompts; FileUpload (`files`, `onFilesChange`, `variant`: dropzone | compact | button) attaches files; ContextRing (`usage: { tokens, contextWindow, percent }`) and UsageNotice (`percent`, `onAction`) show context and quota use. - InlineDiff (`source`) and DiffTable (`columns`, `rows`, `addedRows`) show proposed changes; CodeBlock and Markdown render code and markdown on their own; AgentLoader, Loader, and TextShimmer are loading states; AiImage shows a generated image with a fallback.
